result:
I found 3 real bugs in `twisted.mail.imap4` and wrote a report for each. I tested 8 properties; the two `MessageSet` properties (round-trip through `str()`/`parseIdList`, and `len`/iteration/`in` matching a reference set) passed.

| # | Bug | Severity | Report |
|---|-----|----------|--------|
| 1 | **`wildcardToRegexp` passes LIST patterns straight into a regex without escaping them.** `listMailboxes("", "Lists.2024")` also returns `ListsX2024`. The pattern `Work(` raises `re.error`. A client-supplied `(A+)+$` took about 2 s against a 27-character mailbox name, so any logged-in user can stall the server (ReDoS). | High | `bug_report_twisted_mail_imap4_wildcardToRegexp_2026-10-28_13-28_u0tc.md` |
| 2 | **The `imap4-utf-7` codec silently corrupts TAB, CR and LF.** `"a\tb"` encodes to `b"a&-b"`, which decodes back as `"a&b"`. `"é\t"` decodes as `"é"`, and `"\n\x08"` produces output that can't be decoded. The cause is that `modified_base64` reuses Python's standard `utf-7` codec, which writes those characters as-is instead of base64-encoding them. | Medium | `bug_report_twisted_mail_imap4_utf7_encoder_2026-10-28_13-28_j96d.md` |
| 3 | **`splitQuoted` / `parseNestedParens` reject a valid quoted string ending in `\\`.** For example, `"C:\\"` raises `MismatchedQuoting`. Twisted's own `collapseNestedLists` produces exactly that form, so the client can't parse a LIST or ENVELOPE response containing a mailbox name or subject that ends in a backslash. | Medium | `bug_report_twisted_mail_imap4_splitQuoted_2026-10-28_13-28_e6d9.md` |

Each report includes a short patch. With all three applied together (by monkeypatching; the checkout itself is untouched), the failing properties pass and so does the existing `twisted.mail.test.test_imap` suite: 342 successes, 0 failures.

My first `splitQuoted` fix also unescaped backslashes, but that broke 2 existing tests. Those tests require backslashes to be kept as-is, so that behaviour is intended and I didn't report it. The patch in report 3 only fixes the crash.

Bug 1 is probably the issue this CVE checkout is about: its latest commit is titled "failing test that uses a python regexp".

The reports are in `runs/twisted-imap4_r5/`, and the tests and candidate fixes are in `runs/twisted-imap4_r5/work/` (`test_imap4_pbt.py`, `fixes.py`).
